profile: A meditator and neuroscience student interested in Buddhism, meditation research and the brain.

shelf.title: The Self That Isn't There
shelf.gist: An essay arguing that close inspection of experience does not turn up a fixed self, and that this no-self teaching works alongside the four noble truths to loosen clinging.

shelf.title: The Four Noble Truths, Plainly
shelf.gist: A plain-language explainer walking through each of the four noble truths and why the diagnosis-and-cure structure still resonates.

shelf.title: Zen Mind, Ordinary Mind
shelf.gist: A blog essay on Zen practice arguing that its austere forms are meant to strip away commentary rather than add mystique.

shelf.title: Ten Days of Silence: A Retreat Diary
shelf.gist: A personal diary from a ten-day Theravada retreat, tracking the daily rhythm of practice, boredom, and small breakthroughs.

shelf.title: Metta: The Practice of Loving-Kindness
shelf.gist: An explainer on the loving-kindness practice of metta, its traditional phrases, and what research on it has found so far.

shelf.title: What Happens to the Default Mode Network During Meditation
shelf.gist: A science explainer on how brain-imaging studies link meditation to reduced activity in the default mode network, the brain's mind-wandering circuit.

shelf.title: Training the Mind: Attention and Meditation Research
shelf.gist: A research explainer on how meditation training affects sustained attention and related cognitive tasks, and the mixed evidence behind the claims.

shelf.title: Neuroplasticity and the Meditating Brain
shelf.gist: An essay on what long-term meditation studies suggest about neuroplasticity, structural brain change, and the limits of the current evidence.

shelf.title: Inside the Lab: EEG Studies of Monks
shelf.gist: A news report on laboratory EEG studies of experienced monks, the unusual brainwave patterns recorded, and the practical difficulties of studying elite practitioners.

shelf.title: Mindfulness on the Morning Commute
shelf.gist: A blog post about weaving mindfulness into an ordinary commute, and what changed after a month of treating the bus ride as practice rather than dead time.

shelf.title: A Week at Wat Suan Mokkh: Retreat Diary Two
shelf.gist: A second retreat diary, this one from a forest monastery, tracking heat, insects, loving-kindness practice, and the strange comfort of a fixed daily bell schedule.

shelf.title: Sitting With Science: A Tour of Meditation Research
shelf.gist: An overview piece touring the current state of meditation research across brain imaging, attention testing, and clinical trials, and what remains unsettled.
